question: Which policy has the highest premium in our portfolio?
cot: Q: Which policy has the highest premium in our portfolio? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We started the query with a CTE to use a Window function “ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY premium DESC nulls last) AS row_num“ to sort the premiums from highest to lowest of each status and be sure to pull the null values to the end since to return a numeric value is mandatory. Finally, we select the main fields to return “policy_reference, status_group, premium, row_num“ from our CTE and select the first already-ordered result. The query SQL is: WITH ranked_premiums AS (SELECT policy_reference, status_group, premium, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY premium DESC nulls last) AS row_num FROM get_premiums()) SELECT policy_reference, status_group, premium, row_num FROM ranked_premiums WHERE row_num = 1 and policy_reference IS NOT NULL ORDER BY status_group;
sql_query: WITH ranked_premiums AS (SELECT policy_reference, status_group, premium, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY premium DESC nulls last) AS row_num FROM get_premiums()) SELECT policy_reference, status_group, premium, row_num FROM ranked_premiums WHERE row_num = 1 and policy_reference IS NOT NULL ORDER BY status_group;

This CTE lists all policy references, indicating the status_group in which they are and the risk_location for each one. A second CTE called 'ranked_premiums' is used, to use a Window function 'ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY risk_location ORDER BY premium DESC nulls last) AS row_num'. question: What is the premium trend over the last [X months/years]?
cot: CoT: Q: What is the premium trend over the last [X months/years]? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We started the query with a CTE called 'premiums' which joins our PostgreSQL custom function 'get_premiums()' with the table 'policies_policymodel' which contains all the policies created into the platform. The field we want to extract from the table policies_policymodel is the bound_date, and we will use the PostgreSQL internal function called 'date_trunc' to extract the month from the bound_date. Finally we select the main fields to return 'period, premium' from our CTE and will use the Window function 'LAG' to access the data from the previous row in the same result set. The LAG function helps us to calculate the premium growth between the current month and the previous one. At the end we simply group all premium by the month extracted from the bound_date. The SQL query is: WITH PREMIUMS AS (SELECT gp.policy_reference, gp.status_group, gp.premium, DATE_TRUNC('month', pm.bound_date) AS period FROM get_premiums() gp LEFT JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON gp.policy_id = pm.id) SELECT period, status_group, SUM(premium) AS gross_premium, LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) AS previous_gross_premium, SUM(premium) - LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) AS gross_premium_growth, ((SUM(premium) - LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period)) / LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) * 100.0)::NUMERIC(32, 2) AS growth_percentage FROM premiums GROUP BY period, status_group ORDER BY period ASC;
sql_query: WITH PREMIUMS AS (SELECT gp.policy_reference, gp.status_group, gp.premium, DATE_TRUNC('month', pm.bound_date) AS period FROM get_premiums() gp LEFT JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON gp.policy_id = pm.id) SELECT period, status_group, SUM(premium) AS gross_premium, LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) AS previous_gross_premium, SUM(premium) - LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) AS gross_premium_growth, ((SUM(premium) - LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period)) / LAG(SUM(premium)) OVER (PARTITION BY status_group ORDER BY period) * 100.0)::NUMERIC(32, 2) AS growth_percentage FROM premiums GROUP BY period, status_group ORDER BY period ASC;

question: Which is our premium share in comparison with the total bound GWP?
cot: CoT: Q: Which is our premium share in comparison with the total bound GWP? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We started the query with a CTE called 'premiums' which joins our PostgreSQL custom function 'get_premiums()' with the tables policies_policymodel which contains all the policies created into the platform and the table policies_limitmodel where we can find the two fields needed to calculate the requested field 'premium_share'. The two fields needed to calculate the 'premium_sare' are the total_layer_premium and share placed into the policies_limitmodel. In addition we are filtering all the policies by status bound, using the status field placed into the policies_policymodel table. Finally, we select the main fields to return 'premium, premium_share' from our CTE and will use them to do the operations. The SQL query is: WITH PREMIUMS AS (SELECT gp.policy_id, gp.policy_reference, gp.premium, (SELECT SUM((plm.total_layer_premium::NUMERIC * plm.share) / 100.0) FROM policies_policymodel pm LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel plm ON pm.id = plm.policy_id WHERE reference = gp.policy_reference AND pm.id = gp.policy_id) AS premium_share FROM get_premiums() gp LEFT JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON gp.policy_id = pm.id WHERE pm.status = 'bound') SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium (bound)", SUM(premium_share) AS "total premium share (bound)", (SUM(premium_share) / SUM(premium)) * 100.0 AS "premium share percentage" FROM premiums;

question: What percentage of policies are above [a certain premium threshold]?
cot: CoT: Q: What percentage of policies are above 1000$ premium? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium The query with a CTE _threshold that sets the premium threshold to be compared with. Then, select all the premiums from get_premiums() function to get all policies with a join to the _threshold CTE for making calculations. We perform a count on the policy_id, select the threshold to show it in the final answer and make two calculus: policies_above_threshold: integer that holds the number of policies with premium above the threshold policies_above_threshold_percentage: numeric value that holds the percentage of the policies_above_threshold vs the total_policies. Finally select the status_group field. The SQL query is: WITH _threshold AS (SELECT 1000 AS threshold) SELECT COUNT(cp.policy_id) AS total_policies, th.threshold AS threshold, COUNT(CASE WHEN cp.premium >= th.threshold THEN 1 END) AS policies_above_threshold, ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN cp.premium >= th.threshold THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(cp.policy_reference)), 2) AS policies_above_threshold_percentage, status_group FROM get_premiums() cp JOIN _threshold th ON TRUE WHERE cp.policy_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY th.threshold, status_group;
sql_query: WITH _threshold AS (SELECT 1000 AS threshold) SELECT COUNT(cp.policy_id) AS total_policies, th.threshold AS threshold, COUNT(CASE WHEN cp.premium >= th.threshold THEN 1 END) AS policies_above_threshold, ROUND((COUNT(CASE WHEN cp.premium >= th.threshold THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(cp.policy_reference)), 2) AS policies_above_threshold_percentage, status_group FROM get_premiums() cp JOIN _threshold th ON TRUE WHERE cp.policy_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY th.threshold, status_group;

question: Can you compare the premium performance of this year vs. last year?
cot: CoT: Q: Can you compare the premium performance of this year vs. last year? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We select all the premiums from get_premiums() function to get all policies. We construct the CTE premium_by_year to summarize the premiums by each year, filtering out the premiums that don’t have a bound_date. We apply the SQL LAG function to calculate the premium_previous_year. Finally we compare the premium_by_year vs the premium_previous_year. The resultant percentage is the premium_growth. The SQL query is: WITH premium_by_year AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date) AS bound_year, SUM(cp.premium) AS premium_by_year FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id WHERE DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date) IS NOT NULL GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date)) SELECT bound_year, premium_by_year, LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year) AS premium_previous_year, (premium_by_year - LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year)) / LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year) * 100 AS premium_growth FROM premium_by_year;
sql_query: WITH premium_by_year AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date) AS bound_year, SUM(cp.premium) AS premium_by_year FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id WHERE DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date) IS NOT NULL GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('year', bound_date)) SELECT bound_year, premium_by_year, LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year) AS premium_previous_year, (premium_by_year - LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year)) / LAG(premium_by_year) OVER (ORDER BY bound_year) * 100 AS premium_growth FROM premium_by_year;

question: What are the top 5 regions/states contributing to premium revenue?
cot: CoT: Q: What are the top 5 regions/states contributing to premium revenue? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We select all the premiums from get_premiums() function to get all policies. Then, we perform several joins: policies_policymodel: to get more details of the policy, such as the policy status policies_locationmodel: to get the location details of the policy We select the grouped fields status and risk_location and the aggregated sum of the premium. Note that risk_location is the result of SQL COALESCE function between the countries_list and the states_list from table policies_locationmodel. It is this way because for US policies the countries_list will be NULL and the states_list a list of the insured US states. Query results are ordered by sum of the premium descendant and we limit to the first 5 results. The SQL query is: SELECT pm.status, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location, sum(cp.premium) as premium FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON pm.id = cp.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id WHERE pm.status IN ('bound', 'expired') GROUP BY pm.status, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) ORDER BY sum(cp.premium) DESC LIMIT 5;
sql_query: SELECT pm.status, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location, sum(cp.premium) as premium FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON pm.id = cp.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id WHERE pm.status IN ('bound', 'expired') GROUP BY pm.status, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) ORDER BY sum(cp.premium) DESC LIMIT 5;

question: What is the premium retention rate for renewals?
cot: CoT: Q: What is the premium retention rate for renewals? A: From table policies_policymodel we need to compute two values first: number of renewal policies: this is the count of renewed policies in bound status. Filters applied are transaction_type = 'renewal', status = 'bound' and version = 0. The policy version (named version) must be 0 to select the original policy always (if not, we could get this number by adding to this calculus the endorsed policies) number of total policies: this is the total number of bound policies. Also here is needed to filter by version = 0 Finally, we just compute the percentage between the number of renewal policies and the number of total policies. The query SQL is: SELECT 'renewal' AS premium_type, (SELECT COUNT(id) FROM policies_policymodel WHERE transaction_type = 'renewal' AND status = 'bound' AND version = 0) / (SELECT COUNT(id) FROM policies_policymodel WHERE status = 'bound' AND version = 0) * 100.0 AS premium_retention_rate;
sql_query: SELECT 'renewal' AS premium_type, (SELECT COUNT(id) FROM policies_policymodel WHERE transaction_type = 'renewal' AND status = 'bound' AND version = 0) / (SELECT COUNT(id) FROM policies_policymodel WHERE status = 'bound' AND version = 0) * 100.0 AS premium_retention_rate;

question: How much premium is lost due to cancellations?
cot: CoT: Q: How much premium is lost due to cancellations? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium We need to filter for policies with status cancelled. Then, compute the number of days between the internal expiry date and the cancellation date and divide it for the subtraction between the internal expiry date and the inception date. Then, get the premium for the lost policies, which have status declined or not taken up. The SQL query is: WITH PREMIUMS AS (SELECT CASE WHEN pm.status NOT IN ('declined', 'not-taken-up') THEN gp.premium END AS premium FROM get_premiums() gp LEFT JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON gp.policy_id = pm.id) SELECT SUM(premium) AS "premium lost due to cancellations" FROM PREMIUMS;

question: How much premium is lost due to declinations or not taken-up policies?
cot: CoT: Q: How much premium is lost due to declinations or not taken-up policies? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. Then, get the premium for the lost policies, which have status declined or not taken up. Then, perform an aggregate sum of each column individually and finally subtract the lost policies premiums from the active policies. The SQL query is: WITH PREMIUMS AS (SELECT CASE WHEN pm.status NOT IN ('declined', 'not-taken-up') THEN gp.premium END AS premium, CASE WHEN pm.status IN ('declined', 'not-taken-up') THEN gp.premium END AS lost_premium FROM get_premiums() gp LEFT JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON gp.policy_id = pm.id) SELECT SUM(premium) - SUM(lost_premium) AS premium_lost_due_to_declinations_or_not_taken_up FROM PREMIUMS;

question: What is the premium at risk if policies are cancelled in the next 30/60/90 days?
cot: CoT: Q: What is the premium at risk if policies are cancelled in the next 30/60/90 days? A: The primary data is provided through the custom PostgreSQL function 'get_premiums()'. This custom function internally calculates the premium of the policy and returns: policy_id : This is the policy identifier policy_reference: This is the reference of the policy is_endorsement : Boolean field which indicates if the policy is an endorsement or not status_group : which has 2 options 'written' and 'not_written' premium: the amount of the policy premium From the get_premiums CTE, we build another CTE with policies filtered by status bound and not cancelled yet (cancelation_date is null). Then, we build 3 more CTEs to get the premium at risk for a 30, 60, and 90-day range. Filter applied on the expiry_date on each CTE to get the corresponding premium at risk on the next 30, 60, and 90 days from today. The SQL query is: WITH get_active_premiums AS (SELECT cp.premium, pm.status, pm.cancellation_date, pm.expiry_date FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id WHERE pm.status = 'bound' AND cancellation_date IS NULL), expiry_30 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 30 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '30 days'), expiry_60 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 60 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '60 days'), expiry_90 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 90 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '90 days') SELECT * FROM expiry_30, expiry_60, expiry_90;
sql_query: WITH get_active_premiums AS (SELECT cp.premium, pm.status, pm.cancellation_date, pm.expiry_date FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id WHERE pm.status = 'bound' AND cancellation_date IS NULL), expiry_30 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 30 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '30 days'), expiry_60 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 60 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '60 days'), expiry_90 AS (SELECT SUM(premium) AS "total premium at risk 90 days" FROM get_active_premiums WHERE status IS NOT NULL AND expiry_date NOT BETWEEN current_date AND current_date + INTERVAL '90 days') SELECT * FROM expiry_30, expiry_60, expiry_90;

question: How does the premium for policy RE2500547 compare to similar policies?
cot: Q: How does the premium for policy RE2500547 compare to similar policies? A: To compare the premium for policy RE2500547 with similar policies, we first fetch the details of the policy, including the premium, layer limit, line of business, segment, and risk location. We then find similar policies that share these characteristics, such as having the same line of business, segment, and risk location, or a layer limit within 5% of the reference policy. We exclude the reference policy from the results and ensure that the policies have the same status ('bound'). The SQL query to achieve this is: WITH _policy_reference AS (SELECT 'RE2500547' AS policy_reference), _policy AS (SELECT pm.id AS policy_id, pm.reference AS policy_reference, pm.status, cp.premium, plm.total_layer_limit AS layer_limit, elob.name AS line_of_business, elobs.name AS segment, plmm.id AS risk_location_id, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN _policy_reference _pr ON cp.policy_reference = _pr.policy_reference INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel plm ON pm.id = plm.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_lines_of_business plob ON plm.id = plob.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lineofbusinessmodel elob ON plob.lineofbusinessmodel_id = elob.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_segments plms ON plm.id = plms.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lobsegmentmodel elobs ON plms.lobsegmentmodel_id = elobs.id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id WHERE pm.status = 'bound') SELECT pm.reference AS policy_reference, pm.status, cp.premium, plm.total_layer_limit AS layer_limit, elob.name AS line_of_business, elobs.name AS segment, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel plm ON pm.id = plm.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_lines_of_business plob ON plm.id = plob.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lineofbusinessmodel elob ON plob.lineofbusinessmodel_id = elob.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_segments plms ON plm.id = plms.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lobsegmentmodel elobs ON plms.lobsegmentmodel_id = elobs.id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id INNER JOIN _policy _p ON pm.status = _p.status AND (plm.total_layer_limit BETWEEN (1 - 0.05) * _p.layer_limit AND (1 + 0.05) * _p.layer_limit OR elob.name = _p.line_of_business OR elobs.name = _p.segment OR plmm.id = _p.risk_location_id) AND pm.status = 'bound' ORDER BY CASE WHEN pm.reference = _p.policy_reference THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, cp.premium DESC;
sql_query: WITH _policy_reference AS (SELECT 'RE2500547' AS policy_reference), _policy AS (SELECT pm.id AS policy_id, pm.reference AS policy_reference, pm.status, cp.premium, plm.total_layer_limit AS layer_limit, elob.name AS line_of_business, elobs.name AS segment, plmm.id AS risk_location_id, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN _policy_reference _pr ON cp.policy_reference = _pr.policy_reference INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel plm ON pm.id = plm.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_lines_of_business plob ON plm.id = plob.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lineofbusinessmodel elob ON plob.lineofbusinessmodel_id = elob.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_segments plms ON plm.id = plms.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lobsegmentmodel elobs ON plms.lobsegmentmodel_id = elobs.id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id WHERE pm.status = 'bound') SELECT pm.reference AS policy_reference, pm.status, cp.premium, plm.total_layer_limit AS layer_limit, elob.name AS line_of_business, elobs.name AS segment, COALESCE(plmm.countries_list, plmm.states_list) AS risk_location FROM get_premiums() cp INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON cp.policy_id = pm.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel plm ON pm.id = plm.policy_id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_lines_of_business plob ON plm.id = plob.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lineofbusinessmodel elob ON plob.lineofbusinessmodel_id = elob.id LEFT JOIN policies_limitmodel_segments plms ON plm.id = plms.limitmodel_id LEFT JOIN entities_lobsegmentmodel elobs ON plms.lobsegmentmodel_id = elobs.id LEFT JOIN policies_locationmodel plmm ON pm.id = plmm.policy_id INNER JOIN _policy _p ON pm.status = _p.status AND (plm.total_layer_limit BETWEEN (1 - 0.05) * _p.layer_limit AND (1 + 0.05) * _p.layer_limit OR elob.name = _p.line_of_business OR elobs.name = _p.segment OR plmm.id = _p.risk_location_id) AND pm.status = 'bound' ORDER BY CASE WHEN pm.reference = _p.policy_reference THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, cp.premium DESC;

question: Has the premium for policy RE2500547 changed over time?
cot: Q: Has the premium for policy RE2500547 changed over time? A: We build a reference CTE named policy_reference that holds the policy reference user has asked about. Then, we select the policies from table _policies _policymodel related to this reference and displaying: id: policy_id, version: policy versioning id. 0 means original policy, 1 means first endorsement policy, etc, original_policy_without_endorsement_id: id of the original policy (the one that has version=0), previous_policy_of_endorsement_id: id of previous policy from which the endorsement has been created, inception_date: date where policy takes action, expiry_date: date when policy expires, status: current policy status, premium: policy amount. The SQL query is: WITH _policy_reference AS (SELECT 'RE2500021' AS reference) SELECT pm.id, pm.version, pm.original_policy_without_endorsement_id, pm.previous_policy_of_endorsement_id, pm.inception_date, pm.expiry_date, pm.status, total_gross_premium(pm.id) AS premium FROM _policy_reference _pr INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON _pr.reference = pm.reference ORDER BY pm.version ASC;
sql_query: WITH _policy_reference AS (SELECT 'RE2500021' AS reference) SELECT pm.id, pm.version, pm.original_policy_without_endorsement_id, pm.previous_policy_of_endorsement_id, pm.inception_date, pm.expiry_date, pm.status, total_gross_premium(pm.id) AS premium FROM _policy_reference _pr INNER JOIN policies_policymodel pm ON _pr.reference = pm.reference ORDER BY pm.version ASC;
